title: Normalized quotient pivot loci, transition cocycles and glued quotient
statement:
Let $N,r$ be integers with $0<r<N$, and let $\mathcal I$ be the increasing $r$-subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Put $B=\mathbf Z[p_J:J\in\mathcal I]$, with every $p_J$ of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For an arbitrary ordered $r$-tuple, let $p_{j_1\ldots j_r}$ be the sorting sign times the corresponding increasing coordinate, or zero if indices repeat. For $I,K\in\mathcal I$ define
$$C_{I,K}(a,b)=p_{i_1\ldots i_{a-1}k_bi_{a+1}\ldots i_r},\qquad F_{I,K}=p_I^{r-1}p_K-\det C_{I,K}.$$
Here determinants use [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Put $H=(F_{I,K}:I,K\in\mathcal I)$, $A=B/H$ with its induced grading [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $X=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], with $U_I=D_+(p_I)$. On $U_I$ let $M^{(I)}$ be the $r\times N$ matrix with identity columns indexed by $I$ and off-pivot entries
$$x^{(I)}_{aj}=p_{i_1\ldots i_{a-1}ji_{a+1}\ldots i_r}/p_I\quad(j\notin I).$$
On every overlap $U_I\cap U_K$ the matrix $D_{IK}=(M^{(I)})_K$ has unit determinant $p_K/p_I$, and
$$M^{(K)}=g_{IK}M^{(I)},\qquad g_{IK}=D_{IK}^{-1},\qquad g_{IL}=g_{KL}g_{IK},\qquad g_{II}=1.$$
The cocycle identity holds on each triple overlap. There exist a locally free rank-$r$ module $Q_X$ and a surjection $q_X:\mathcal O_X^{\oplus N}\twoheadrightarrow Q_X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], with frames $Q_X|_{U_I}\cong\mathcal O_{U_I}^{\oplus r}$ whose transition maps are $g_{IK}$ and in which $q_X$ is the matrix $M^{(I)}$. These local quotient maps have the right inverses given by inclusion of the pivot columns.
Moreover, for every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and surjection $q:\mathcal O_T^{\oplus N}\twoheadrightarrow Q$ onto a locally free rank-$r$ module, the loci $T_I$ where $(q(e_{i_1}),\ldots,q(e_{i_r}))$ is a frame are open and cover $T$. On $T_I$, $q$ has a unique normalized matrix with identity columns at $I$; on $T_I\cap T_K$ changing the frame is left multiplication by the inverse $K$-column matrix. For every morphism $f:T'\to T$, the pivot locus of $f^*q$ is exactly $f^{-1}(T_I)$, and its normalized entries are the pullbacks of those of $q$ [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-plucker-determinant-locus-charts], the $U_I$ cover $X$ and $\det M^{(I)}_J=p_J/p_I$. On $U_I\cap U_K$ the sections $p_K/p_I$ and $p_I/p_K$ multiply to $1$, so $d=\det D_{IK}=p_K/p_I$ is a unit. The adjugate identity [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] gives the two-sided inverse $D_{IK}^{-1}=d^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(D_{IK})$. Thus $g_{IK}$ is a well-defined invertible matrix over the structure sheaf of the overlap.

source.place: Tag 089T, lemma-gkn-representable, normalized quotient subfunctors and their open covering; explicit determinant-chart completion by agent.

proof.text:
Put $V=M^{(I)}$ and $W=D_{IK}^{-1}V$ on the overlap. Then $W_K=1$. For any increasing $r$-subset $J$, multiplicativity of determinants [lem-sfb-matrix-cramer-determinant-identities] and the chart minor formula [lem-sfb-plucker-determinant-locus-charts] give
$$\det W_J=(\det D_{IK})^{-1}\det V_J=p_J/p_K.$$
The same formula for an ordered tuple follows by its sorting sign, with both sides zero for repetitions. Replace column $a$ in the identity matrix $W_K$ by column $j$ of $W$. In the determinant expansion every term except the one selecting row $a$ in that column is zero, and the remaining term is $W_{aj}$. Therefore
$$W_{aj}=\det W_{(k_1,\ldots,k_{a-1},j,k_{a+1},\ldots,k_r)}=p_{k_1\ldots k_{a-1}jk_{a+1}\ldots k_r}/p_K.$$
These are exactly the off-pivot entries defining $M^{(K)}$, and both matrices have identity $K$-columns. Hence $M^{(K)}=g_{IK}M^{(I)}$. No cancellation of a nonunit has occurred.

proof.text: On a triple overlap the previous equality twice gives $g_{KL}g_{IK}M^{(I)}=M^{(L)}=g_{IL}M^{(I)}$. Taking the $I$-columns, which form the identity matrix, gives $g_{IL}=g_{KL}g_{IK}$. Also $D_{II}=1$, so $g_{II}=1$; taking $L=I$ gives $g_{KI}g_{IK}=1$. This checks the direction and the diagonal cases of the gluing cocycle.

source.place: Tag 089T, lemma-gkn-representable, normalized quotient subfunctors and their open covering; explicit determinant-chart completion by agent.

proof.text: Apply the sheaf-gluing clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] to $\mathcal F_I=\mathcal O_{U_I}^{\oplus r}$ with isomorphisms $g_{IK}:\mathcal F_I\to\mathcal F_K$. Obtain $Q_X$ and frames $\phi_I:Q_X|_{U_I}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_I$ satisfying $\phi_K=g_{IK}\phi_I$. These frames make $Q_X$ locally free of rank $r$ by [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. The maps $\phi_I^{-1}M^{(I)}$ agree on overlaps, since $M^{(K)}=g_{IK}M^{(I)}$, and clause (1) of the gluing lemma gives a global $q_X$. In the $I$-frame its composite with the inclusion of the $I$-summands is the identity. Consequently every local target section lifts on the cover $U_I$, so $q_X$ is surjective as a sheaf map. The indicated inclusions are precisely the local right inverses in the statement.

source.place: Tags 04TN (lemma-glue-maps), 00AL (lemma-glue-sheaves), 00AM (lemma-glue-sheaves-structures); filling the gluing paragraph of Tag 089T.

proof.text: Now fix $T,Q,q$ as in the statement. On any trivializing open $V$ for $Q$, write $q$ as a matrix $E$. For an index $I$, let $a_I=\det E_I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function], $D_V(a_I)$ is open and $a_I$ has an inverse there. The adjugate identity [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] then inverts $E_I$ on this open, so its ordered columns are a frame. Conversely a frame makes $E_I$ invertible; determinant multiplicativity [lem-sfb-matrix-cramer-determinant-identities] gives that its determinant is a unit. Thus the frame locus on $V$ is exactly $D_V(a_I)$. Changing the trivialization multiplies $E_I$ by an invertible matrix, whose determinant is a unit by the same identity, so this locus is independent of the chosen trivialization. These opens agree on intersections and define the claimed open $T_I$ in $T$.

proof.text:
To prove these opens cover, fix $t\in T$ and a trivialization near $t$. With $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, the finite free stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-module-stalk-equiv] writes $q_t$ as $E_t:R^N\to R^r$. It is surjective by stalk exactness [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], applied to $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus N}\to Q\to0$. Choose a preimage of each of the $r$ basis vectors; their columns form $S:R^r\to R^N$ with $E_tS=1$. Apply the explicit Cauchy--Binet formula in clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors] with $A=S$, $B=E_t$ and $f=1$:
$$1=\sum_{|I|=r}\det((E_t)_I)\det(S_I).$$
Here $S_I$ consists of the $I$-rows and $(E_t)_I$ of the $I$-columns, in increasing order. If every $\det((E_t)_I)$ belonged to the maximal ideal of $R$, this equality would put $1$ in that ideal. Some minor therefore lies outside it. The basic-open criterion [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function] puts $t$ in that $T_I$. This argument uses no assumption that $q$ is surjective on sections of a fixed open.

proof.text: On $T_I$ put $b_I=q\circ s_I:\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$, where $s_I$ includes the pivot summands. Define $E^{(I)}=b_I^{-1}q$. It has identity $I$-columns. Any frame with that normalization has inverse $b_I$, because its inverse sends each standard basis vector to $q(e_{i_a})$; hence the normalized matrix is unique. On $T_I\cap T_K$ put $D=(E^{(I)})_K=b_I^{-1}b_K$. It follows directly that $E^{(K)}=D^{-1}E^{(I)}$. The same identity gives its local right inverse $s_I$ in the normalized frame.

source.place: Tag 089T, lemma-gkn-representable, normalized quotient subfunctors and their open covering; explicit determinant-chart completion by agent.

proof.text: Let $f:T'\to T$. The tensor description of [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies the pullback of a displayed free module with the free module on the same basis: $1\otimes e_a$ corresponds to $e_a$. It identifies the pulled-back matrix on $f^{-1}V$ with the entrywise image of $E$ under $f^\sharp$. Thus its $I$-minor is the image of $a_I$ (apply the determinant's finite sum formula). At a point $t'\mapsto t$, the stalk homomorphism is local by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. A unit maps to a unit; a nonunit lies in the maximal ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion] and maps into the maximal ideal, so remains a nonunit. The basic-open criterion [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function] therefore gives $T'_I=f^{-1}(T_I)$. On these opens $f^*b_I$ is the pivot frame, so the pulled-back entries of $b_I^{-1}q$ are exactly the normalized entries of $f^*q$. The inverse is preserved because the images of the two identities $b_Ib_I^{-1}=1=b_I^{-1}b_I$ are the corresponding identities after pullback. Finally, the pulled-back pivot inclusions are right inverses on the inverse-image cover, ensuring that $f^*q$ is itself a surjection onto a locally free rank-$r$ module.
